Triage: lands in `packages/plugins/plugin-security` (the #5492 `owner_only_writes` floor stays composed into Layer 1 because `ISharingService` abstains on a `public_read_write` object, and per the documented composition an abstain keeps the floor — contradicting the OWD contract that declares writes open). Stays `domain:identity`; queued `pm:queue`.

Rationale: only failing cell of a 124-cell matrix re-drive, with two independent mechanism confirmations (`/security/explain` reporting `narrows` with zero authored RLS; the cross-object creator-vs-non-creator PATCH split). The filer honestly flags that attribution to the `92f26f75 → b602d536` window lacks a build ablation — the dev should reproduce first, per the card.

Acceptance is well-specified on the card, including the non-regression edges: the object-level gate's distinct refusal, the `created_by` floor on `private`/`public_read` objects, and #7792's by-id write-visibility behaviour.

Container & model: **M**, `mode:subagent`, `model: opus` — per the 2026-08-12 backend ruling (S-mechanical + M ⇒ subagent; cloud reserved for L/XL, work outliving the PM session, browser/dogfood verification, build-heavy M). The reproduction here is HTTP-level against a booted app and the regression surface is this package's own dogfood/matrix test files, so none of the cloud reservations apply. `opus` because the composition semantics are a judgement call on a security boundary, not a mechanical edit.
Serial constraints cleared: `plugin-security` is **free** — no in-flight claim in this lane touches it. Both of this lane's in-flight PRs are in other packages and are now armed and in the queue: #7974 (`plugin-sharing/src/share-link-service.ts`) and #8017 (`plugin-auth`). ⚠️ The three other `plugin-sharing` queue cards (#7807, #7858, #7795) stay held behind #7974 reaching MERGED, and #7994 behind #8017 — none of them is this card, and none overlaps this file surface.

## Premise re-verified on current `origin/main` before claiming

The card was filed 11:50Z today, so it is fresh, but the floor it names had to be confirmed rather than assumed:

- `owner_only_writes` (object `'*'`, operation `update`, `using: created_by == current_user.id`) **still exists** and is still seeded — `objects/default-permission-sets.ts:415`.
- Last touch to either named file is `9a75790` (#7916, the `$field` RLS / analytics change). Nothing has landed since that would have already moved this behaviour.

⚠️ **One correction to the card's own file attribution, carried into the dispatch:** the card cites `platform-ownership-policies.ts` as the policy's home. That file *documents* the floor (line 11), but the shipped seed is in `objects/default-permission-sets.ts:415`. A dev that edits only the cited file would change a comment and ship nothing.

## Why this is dispatchable rather than escalated

The access matrix declares `edit: true`, `/meta/object` reports `sharingModel: 'public_read_write'`, and no RLS is authored — three declarations agreeing, and the platform answering 403. That is a **declared-≠-enforced defect on a published surface**, i.e. restoring an invariant the platform already states, which is the named immediate-action class. It does not widen an accept set by design; it makes the runtime match the OWD contract.

⚠️ It is nonetheless a **write-authorization boundary**, so the acceptance edges are non-negotiable and all four go into the dispatch verbatim — in particular that the `created_by` floor must **still refuse** non-owner writes on `private` / `public_read` objects. A fix that opens writes everywhere would satisfy the headline symptom and be a security regression.

| check | result |

| The load-bearing placement claim | ✅ the drop is inside `computeLayeredRlsFilter` at collection time, keyed on the **declared** `sharingModel`, not on `effectiveSharingModel` |

## The two judgements that make this a good fix rather than a passing one

**The placement.** You could have satisfied the headline symptom at `dropPlatformOwnershipFloor` further down and every acceptance case would still have gone green — and it would have compiled Layer 1 to `null` and handed back an **ungated by-id write**, reopening the hole #7665 closed. Fixing one security bug by reopening another is the single most expensive outcome available on this card, and the thing that caught it was `[D]` failing on its *first* assertion during ablation, exactly as predicted. That is the predict-then-mutate discipline earning its cost.

**Declared, not effective.** Reading `effectiveSharingModel` would have folded `controlled_by_parent` and unset-model `sys_*` tables into the same `public` bucket and opened cross-creator writes on the platform's identity tables — as a side effect of a fix for app objects. That is the invisible-widening shape review is worst at catching. Keying on the author's declaration keeps *declared = enforced* exact.

## Your open question — A confirmed, and it was right to ask

**A. Only an explicit `sharingModel: 'public_read_write'` drops the floor; `sys_*` unset-model objects keep it.** Your reasoning holds on all three axes and I'll add the decisive one: **an unset model is a legacy default, not a statement**, and ADR-0090 D1 already ruled that direction unsafe on the read axis after a real incident. Deriving a *write* grant from a default the platform has already decided cannot be trusted would re-litigate that ruling sideways, on the more dangerous axis, without anyone deciding to. The card cites the `sys_user_position` split as **evidence of the mechanism**, not as a requirement — and its acceptance criteria never mention it. If cross-creator writes are ever wanted on a system table, the honest route is to declare it on that object.

⛔ No follow-up card. This is a settled boundary, not a deferred one.

## One consequence I want on the record, since it is a real behaviour change

You flagged it and you were right to: on a `public_read_write` object where sharing answers **`allow`** (ownership-at-depth / edit share / `modifyAllRecords`), the write is now **also** gated by the caller's derived select scope, where previously it was not. That is a **narrowing**, it is consistent with #7665's "you cannot mutate what you cannot see", and `[D]` covers it. Accepted deliberately rather than noticed later — a narrowing on a write path is the safe direction, and it is now pinned.

## The fixture finding is the most valuable thing in this report

> *"my first fixture was org-less and passed on the broken build"*

The floor is positions-gated to `org_member`, which a principal holds only through a `sys_member` row — so in an org-less harness the PATCH answers **200 and the defect is invisible**. A fixture that cannot fail is worse than no fixture, and you caught yours by ablating rather than by reading it. That precondition is absent from the card, so anyone re-running the QA matrix org-less would have recorded this cell as passing.

⚠️ **That is a testing-harness gap larger than this card**, so I am not letting it die in a PR body: filing it as a `finding` against the QA checklist path, where the grading is the triage seat's call and not mine.

## Next steps (mine)

CI was `in_progress` at review time — `Build Core` ✅, `Dogfood Verify CLI` ✅, with Test Core, Dogfood Regression 1–3/3, TypeScript Type Check and ESLint still running. I will read the **per-job conclusions** (⛔ never the aggregate — `get_status` on this repo returns only a Vercel status and reads `success` while saying nothing about any gate), then flip ready and arm. The stale-`dist` lap you hit is worth remembering repo-wide: after restoring a source file, a re-run without a rebuild gives a **false red**.
